subject: Short diagnostic snapshot request — NovaPay incident 2027-11-15
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@novapay.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 22:03:00 +1100
Subject: Short diagnostic snapshot request — production error 11/15

Hi Hannah,

We just saw a spike of 5xx errors in our production integration with Redwood between ~21:42–21:58 AEDT. We captured a few failed requests that look like they might be upstream timeouts, but our engineers need a short-term snapshot of the tenant-level request traces and the KV cache metadata to correlate with our service logs.

Can Redwood provide a read-only, timeboxed snapshot (app-level traces + kv-metadata) for the window 2027-11-15T21:40:00+11:00 to 2027-11-15T22:00:00+11:00? Preferably exported as a sanitized TAR that excludes cleartext PII and system keys. We need the data for forensic triage; if possible we’d like access for our engineers for up to 72 hours.

Attached is our internal incident report and a signed customer access request form (nova_snapshot_request_form.pdf). We can sign any short addendum you need.

Thanks — urgent for us.

Tom Li
Head of SRE, NovaPay
support-it@novapay.com

Folks — forwarding Tom's ask from NovaPay. They want a short-lived, read-only snapshot of traces + KV metadata for a 20-minute window to help their triage. They propose up to 72 hours access.

My immediate asks:
- Security (Soojin): any blockers for a timeboxed export and direct access to sanitized artifacts?
- Engineering (Dev): what is the minimal extract we can provide that avoids PII and still lets them triage? Can we generate a sanitized replay?
- Ops (Grace): what audit controls / ACL changes would be needed and can we enforce an automatic deletion after the window?

Constraints I'd like to propose in the meantime:
- Max 48 hr access rather than 72; read-only, no export of raw S3 objects containing keys;
- Produce a sanitized TAR that strips user identifiers and hashes request metadata;
- KMS audit log capture + ticket (SUP-4721) + DocuSign addendum before access.

Attaching a suggested sanitization checklist and a shell to extract minimal traces (sanitization_checklist.md, minimal_trace_extractor.sh). If you can triage this today, please reply with a short approval/conditions and I'll communicate to the customer.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 16, 2027 at 00:12 -08:00, hannah_schmitt wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Tom's ask from NovaPay. They want a short-lived, read-only snapshot...

We can do this, but with careful sanitization. Quick technical summary:
- Minimal payload: request/response headers, timestamp, model id, token counts, KV cache metadata (per-tenant), and request IDs. No request bodies that contain user-generated content unless NovaPay explicitly needs a subset and signs an additional approval.
- Sanitization approach: replace user identifiers and account ids with stable tokens (hashes), redact Authorization strings and any bearer tokens.
- Delivery: create a read-only S3 prefix in the APAC region with object ACLs set to internal-root + temporary NovaPay role; pre-signed URLs are allowed for up to 48 hours.
- Auditing: enable KMS key-use audit and attach access logs. We'll also snapshot the runtime config used during the window.

Estimated time to produce: 3–4 hours to run extraction, another 1 hour to validate sanitization. I attached the extractor script (minimal_trace_extractor.sh) — it outputs a sanitized tarball and a sanitization log.

If Legal/Security insist on a signed DPA addendum, we should gate release until that is completed, but we can stage the artifact and enable access after DocuSign completes.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: minimal_trace_extractor.sh (script)
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 13:49:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Short diagnostic snapshot request — production error 11/15

Thanks for the context and proposed controls. Quick position: we can approve a timeboxed diagnostic snapshot with the following mandatory conditions — please don’t release anything until these are in place.

1) Timebox: access limited to 48 hours. No extensions without a renewed approval from Security + Legal.
2) Scope: only the minimal sanitized artifacts Dev described (no raw request bodies unless explicitly approved and justified in writing).
3) Legal addendum: NovaPay must sign a short access addendum (DocuSign link below) that includes a clause acknowledging data minimization and acceptance of audit logs.
4) Audit & KMS: all access must be logged at the KMS level and logs preserved for 180 days for this ticket.
5) Ticketing: create SUP-4721 (already suggested) and attach the tar + sanitization log and the deletion confirmation once the 48 hr window closes.
6) Ops guardrail: enforce object lifecycle rule to auto-delete the S3 prefix 48 hours after grant; set ACL to revoke role immediately after expiry.

If you can stage the artifact in a restricted prefix and start the DocuSign flow, Security will sign off. Grace/Dev — once staged, please ping me with the SUP ticket and the pre-signed access details.

Soojin Lee
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
